tts: These sneakers sell over three billion Swiss francs a year. And they started with a garden hose.
For decades, big brands fought over the perfect sole: air, gel, softer and softer foam.
But a sole that's too soft feels mushy when you push off.
Swiss triathlete Olivier Bernhard cut a garden hose into pieces and glued them under his shoe.
When your foot lands, the pieces squash and soak up the impact. Once they're fully compressed, they turn firm, and you push off like from a board.
Big brands reportedly weren't interested. So in twenty ten, he and two friends founded On, in Zurich.
In twenty nineteen, Roger Federer invested. And in twenty twenty-one, On went public, valued at over eleven billion dollars.
Last year, sales grew thirty percent. That's what happens when you look at an ordinary hose and ask: what if?
